```python
def words_string(s):
    """
    You will be given a string of words separated by commas or spaces. Your task is
    to split the string into words and return an array of the words.
    
    For example:
    words_string("Hi, my name is John") == ["Hi", "my", "name", "is", "John"]
    words_string("One, two, three, four, five, six") == ["One", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six"]
    """
    return s.replace(",", " ").split()
```
message.reasoning_content:
The task is to split a string by commas or spaces and return a list of words.

I can replace commas with spaces, then split by whitespace. This handles both cases cleanly.

```python
def words_string(s):
    return s.replace(",", " ").split()
```

This works because:
- "Hi, my name is John" → "Hi  my name is John" → ["Hi", "my", "name", "is", "John"]
- "One, two, three, four, five, six" → "One  two  three  four  five  six" → ["One", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six"]

The `.split()` without arguments splits on any whitespace and ignores multiple consecutive spaces, so the double spaces from replacing commas are handled fine.
